_comment: Single machine-readable source of truth for the herdr toolchain pin (#609, epic #667). Read by #390's workspace-doctor check 8 ('herdr binary present AND version == the pinned release'). MUST stay equal to HERDR_VERSION_FLOOR in phase_executor/src/phase_executor/herdr_backend.py — tests/hooks/test_herdr_pin.py asserts it. Verify an install with: sha256sum ~/.local/bin/herdr, compared against gh api repos/<repo>/releases/tags/<tag> asset .digest. Full procedure and rationale: docs/reviews/2026-07-27-609-herdr-supply-chain-vet.md

api_schema._comment: Recorded from `herdr api schema --json` on the pinned binary. #609 only RECORDS this; asserting it against a live server is #390's check 10.

config_baseline._comment: Hardened target for ~/.config/herdr/config.toml. Keys and their upstream defaults were read from `herdr --default-config`, never assumed. manifest_check defaults to TRUE and makes herdr fetch a remote agent-detection manifest from herdr.dev in the background — behavior can change under a pinned binary with no version bump, which is the supply-chain hole a version pin alone does not close. Apply with `herdr config check && herdr server reload-config` (no restart needed). NOT yet applied to this host: owner-triggered per epic-run D-5.

verified.method: gh api repos/ogulcancelik/herdr/releases/tags/v0.7.5 asset .digest (sha256:3dc83288...c59253, size 21315048) compared against sha256sum ~/.local/bin/herdr (3dc83288...c59253) — identical digest AND identical size, so the installed binary is the official release bit-for-bit. Verified in place; no re-download and no re-install, because the live herdr server was backing 4 actively-working sessions.
verified.install_method: pinned release binary verified against its published digest (never curl|sh, which plan 1.6 excludes for this workspace)
